title: Greek Mythology
text: Greek mythology is the body of myths originally told by the ancient Greeks, encompassing their cosmogony, theogony, and a rich pantheon of gods, heroes, and monsters. The twelve Olympian gods, headed by Zeus, ruler of Mount Olympus, included Hera, Athena, Apollo, Artemis, Poseidon, Hephaestus, Ares, Aphrodite, Hermes, Demeter, and Dionysus. Greek myths explained natural phenomena, honored cultural heroes, and served religious and moral purposes. Major mythological narratives include the Trojan War, the Labors of Heracles (Hercules), the Odyssey of Odysseus, the tragedy of Oedipus, and the stories of Perseus and Theseus. Greek mythology profoundly influenced Roman culture and continues to permeate Western art, literature, and language.
